notes: Stage S1 (pilot) of the RQ-H1B resource decision, candidate B: the same grid as `pilot.json` with one axis moved, so an A/B difference has exactly one candidate explanation.
Candidate B differs from candidate A only in `prompt`: it asks one extra recoverability question. RQ-14 froze that candidate; this plan only turns the definition into a run.
Every other member is copied from `pilot.json` on purpose — same cases, same targets, same bounds — because a second variable would make the comparison uninterpretable.

bounds.maxAttempts 70 is this run's exact worst case: 50 decision cells x 1 attempt + 10 chat cells x 2 (one attempt plus the transport's one repair). It is the ceiling, not a reserve. A second pilot pass needs its own run directory and is separately bounded, because --resume only dispatches cells with no record at all and a failed cell keeps its record.

Targets 1-2 are the local Clef service on 127.0.0.1:8000. Their credential references are empty strings on purpose: an endpoint that authenticates nobody is expressed by naming nothing, and the runner then sends no Authorization header at all. A placeholder name would have been sent as a fabricated bearer.
Targets 3-5 name credential references only. No credential value appears in this document; a live run resolves CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and TYPESAFE_API_KEY from the environment.

Target 6 is a chat route reached through the headless HTTP chat service added for this task (evals/src/run/chat-service.ts). `provider` and `model` are the host-observed route ids, not display labels; the service reads DEEPSEEK_API_KEY at call time.
The two workbuddy chat targets in the previous revision are gone: the user removed that route from the pilot, and a headless run has no route for it either.

Two of the ten cases declare their own material incomplete. That is an input fact to measure, not a run failure; no case is truncated at this budget, which is why context.maxInputTokens stays at the production default.

concurrency is 2 rather than 4: no evidence exists for four-way concurrency against these providers, and the pilot's purpose is to measure latency and failure modes, not throughput. Four-way is a later value once 429 behaviour is known.
